selection_rationale: Türkiye is a major NATO, Black Sea, Mediterranean and Middle Eastern actor with deep EU manufacturing integration, yet the public corpus lacked a reusable country dossier connecting its inflation and exchange-rate regime, manufacturing structure, energy dependence, defence industry, refugee system, earthquake reconstruction and strategic geography. Existing Europe–Russia–Ukraine, Russia, Iran and Saudi Arabia research all require Turkish context to avoid reconstructing the same transmission mechanisms.
contrary_evidence: Inflation above 30% and recurring lira volatility support a macroeconomic-instability thesis, while low public debt, a functioning banking system, manufacturing exports and large tourism receipts argue against a sovereign or institutional-collapse narrative.
EU accession negotiations remain stalled, but the EU absorbs over two-fifths of Turkish goods exports and Customs Union cooperation continued to deepen in 2026.
Domestic gas, LNG infrastructure and renewables improve energy security, while natural-gas imports still represented roughly 95% of 2025 supply.

Defence exports above US$10 billion demonstrate significant industrial capability, but export value does not establish full technological autonomy because imported components and foreign certifications remain relevant.
limitations: Inflation and growth forecasts changed materially during 2026 and must be attributed to their forecast date rather than averaged.
Turkish official sources are primary for administrative, trade, energy and defence-industry quantities but do not provide independent evaluation of policy performance.
Refugee stocks change through registration, voluntary return, resettlement and status changes; the latest UNHCR headline total used here is a mid-2025 snapshot.
Ethnicity is not comprehensively measured in official statistics, so the dossier avoids unsupported estimates of Kurdish or other ethnic population shares.
Defence-export figures are not equivalent to domestic value added or independently verified technological content.
Akkuyu's first unit remained in commissioning preparation at the evidence cutoff; planned generation is not counted as realised power supply.
Revision 1 adds the required evidence-bearing geographic map in both locales with semantic parity; no substantive factual conclusion is changed.

en.title: Türkiye: industrial scale, monetary disinflation and strategic autonomy between Europe and Asia
en.deck: Türkiye combines deep manufacturing, low sovereign debt and strategic geography with still-high inflation, external energy dependence and an unfinished shift toward higher-technology production; the central test is whether current disinflation becomes a durable institutional regime.
en.regime: Large transcontinental manufacturing economy undergoing restrictive disinflation, with low public debt and strong industrial capacity offset by high nominal instability, energy import dependence and large external financing flows.
en.key_risk: Premature monetary easing or a regional energy shock could restart the inflation-lira cycle before expectations and reserves are strong enough to sustain lower inflation.

pt-BR.title: Turquia: escala industrial, desinflação monetária e autonomia estratégica entre Europa e Ásia
pt-BR.deck: A Turquia combina manufatura profunda, dívida soberana baixa e geografia estratégica com inflação ainda elevada, dependência de energia externa e transição incompleta para produção de maior tecnologia; o teste central é transformar a desinflação atual em regime institucional durável.
pt-BR.regime: Grande economia manufatureira transcontinental em desinflação restritiva, com dívida pública baixa e capacidade industrial forte contrabalançadas por instabilidade nominal elevada, dependência de importação de energia e grandes fluxos de financiamento externo.
pt-BR.key_risk: Afrouxamento monetário prematuro ou choque regional de energia pode reiniciar o ciclo inflação-lira antes que expectativas e reservas sejam fortes o suficiente para sustentar inflação menor.
